（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL POLICE FORCE）
POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH.)

December 8th 1915

Sir,
In connection with the attached report the French
Police inform me that No.14 Rue Chapsal is a house
occupied by a Japanese whose rent is paid by the South
Manchurian Railway. His house was a very busy centre
during the evening of the day on which the rebels
seized the cruiser Chisu Ho肇和. The numbers of
men both Chinese and Japanese who streamed in and out
alarmed the neighbours one of whom reported the matter
to the French Police. The Police could do nothing as
the house was that of a Japanese subject.

Your Obedient Servant,
（签名）
Chief Detective Inspector.

日期 16年5月20日
上海工部局。 3757
15年12月14日

（印章：上海工部局警务处）
警务处，
（侦探科。）

1915年12月8日

先生：
就随附报告而言，法国警察告知我，沙普萨尔路（Rue Chapsal）14号是一处由一名日本人居住的房屋，其租金由南满洲铁道株式会社支付。在叛军夺取“肇和”号巡洋舰的当天晚上，该住所是一个非常繁忙的中心。进进出出的中日人士数量之多令邻居们感到惊恐，其中一人向法国警察报告了此事。警方对此无能为力，因为该房屋属于日本臣民。

Form 2    34
Shanghai Municipal Police.    282
                              2875/16
Central Police    Station.
December 8th    1915.
REPORT ON Shadowing of Suspicious Japanese.
Made by D.S. 32 Givens    Forwarded by

Sir,
With reference to my report of this morning,
I now beg to report that the Japanese,
J. Yamada, returned to the Chartered Bank,
and drew the money about 11.30 a.m. He then
went to the South Manchuria Railway Co.,
No. 1 Huikiang Road, where he stayed about
five minutes. On leaving there, he went to
Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, No. 49 Szechuen Road.
The detective, who shadowed him, remained
outside this address till 1.30 p.m. up to which
time, Yamada had not come out.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J. P. Givens
Det. Sergeant.

Chief Detective Inspector.

关于监视可疑日本人的报告。
由侦探警士 32号 吉文斯（Givens）呈报    转呈

先生：
参照我今晨的报告，现谨报告如下：日本人 J. Yamada 返回了有利银行，并于上午11时30分左右提取了款项。随后他前往汇江路1号的南满洲铁道株式会社，在那里停留了约五分钟。离开那里后，他前往四川路49号的三井物产会社。负责监视他的侦探在此地址外守候至下午1时30分，在此期间，Yamada 未曾出来。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
J. P. Givens
侦探警士。

首席侦探督察。

Gonzaleuro 沙普纳尔路（Rue Chaponal）14号
252

Form 2    34
Shanghai Municipal Police.
882
25/5/16
Central Police Station.
December 8th 1915.
REPORT ON Japanese Receiving Money from Straits.
Made by D.S. Givens    Forwarded by

Sir,
I beg to report that, in accordance with your instructions, I proceeded to the Chartered Bank at 10.20 a.m. to-day, when one of the clerks in the bank pointed out to me a Japanese named J. Yamada, who had come to the bank to receive Tls 4,300.00 remitted to him by cable from the Straits. The clerk told me that Yamada has received monetary remittances in the same way from the same place on three or four occasions recently. The cablegrams were addressed "Zungaluro, No. 14 hue bhapeal". Yamada states that this is his telegraphic address, and that he works in South Manchuria Railway Co. On one occasion the cablegram was addressed "Zungaleuro, No. 14 hue bhapeal". On the first occasion that money was remitted to Yamada, the bank had inquiries made at No. 14 hue bhapeal, but nobody there appeared to know anything of "Zungaluro".
After pointing out Yamada to me the bank clerk sent him to the Japanese consulate to get proof of his identity, and I have made arrangements to have him shadowed when he comes back to get the money. The remittances present by a Chinese.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J. S. Givens D.I.
Chief Detective Inspector.

16年5月25日
中央捕房。
1915年12月8日。
关于一名日本人接收来自海峡殖民地汇款的报告。
由侦探警士 吉文斯（Givens）呈报    转呈

先生：
谨报告，遵照您的指示，我于今天上午10时20分前往有利银行，当时银行的一名职员向我指认了一名名为 J. Yamada 的日本人，他来银行收取从海峡殖民地通过电报汇给他的规元银4,300.00两。该职员告诉我，Yamada 最近曾三四次以同样方式从同一地点接收汇款。电报的地址写的是“Zungaluro, No. 14 hue bhapeal”。Yamada 称这是他的电报地址，并声称他在南满洲铁道株式会社工作。有一次，电报地址写的是“Zungaleuro, No. 14 hue bhapeal”。在第一次向 Yamada 汇款时，银行曾向 hue bhapeal 14号进行查询，但那里似乎无人知晓“Zungaluro”为何人。
在向我不出 Yamada 后，银行职员派他去日本领事馆获取身份证明，我已安排在他回来取款时对其进行监视。汇款由一名华人出示。
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
J. S. Givens 侦探督察
首席侦探督察。

pages.en:
Translation of a letter.
FILED
C. I. D.
I. O. REG
No. 982
To brother Ying Sz 英士
(evidently Chen Chi Mei 陳其美),

When we returned to Singapore from Ih Li Ming 日厘棉 (?)
issent you a letter which, we presume, has reached you O.K.
We went to Solo from Po Dah Wei 八打威(?) the day before
yesterday and arrived here (Semarang) yesterday.
There are many rich emigrants here but owing to
their ignorance they would rather sacrifice their lives
than contribute money.
Fortunately good news reached here from home. One or
two enthusiasts opened their purse to the contributions
and this was responded to by others but we can only
expect to collect about thirty thousand dollars and have
no hope to get a bigger amount.
We will depart for Si Seu 泗水 to day and leave Mr.
Tseng here to try to convert one or two capitalists.
This if met with success may result in raising $100,000.
With reference to the place Si Seu 泗水 we learn that
the Chamber of Commerce there has the intention of supporting us.
Judging from this we have reasons to believe that in Java
and other ports although big capitalists will not open their
purse about $100,000 will be raised. But we are unable to
know exactly until we arrive there. In short during our
visit this time to the south in the British and Dutch
Colonies we can raise $150,000 in a month's time.
If in Shanghai and in other parts a rising takes place
we can foresee that the contributions will come
continually.
After our visit to Si Seu 泗水 we intend to return
to Singapore where we will discuss with Do Wen 卓文(Chung
Chi wrote to us saying that Do Wen would come to Singapore
very soon) and then decide our movements. Our opinion
is that a long stay in this place is not suitable at all.
The proverb has it "One can only become a guest temporarily
and not permanently." If we stay long others would feel
uneasy and besides owing to unsatisfactory communications
we are at a loss to know what has happened or is going on
in our motherland. It is also not good if we return.
Tih Sun 狄引民 ) has sent many others to return (? to China).
We are roaming about here much against our will and also
against the will of others.
Since we left you we have not yet been favoured with your
news from the interior which we regret. We hope that on
receiving this letter you will send us a telegram.
Perhaps, if you order us to return it may help in awakening
the people and arousing them to find others to replace us.
The contributions raised in British Colonies will be sent
to Shanghai while the money raised in Dutch Colonies will
be sent to Tokio.
As you always communicate with those in Tokio you must
know all about it. Since our movements are uncertain
we cannot tell you all we desire to say. Excuse us.
With compliments.
Ching 銓 and Tsai 智 .

December 2nd.
From Semarang.

信件译文。
归档
刑事侦缉处
情报登记
编号 982
致英士兄 英士
（显然是陈其美），

当我们从 Ih Li Ming 日厘棉 (?) 返回新加坡时，曾给您去信一封，想必已顺利送达。
前天我们从 Po Dah Wei 八打威(?) 前往梭罗（Solo），并于昨天抵达此处（三宝垄）。
此处有许多富有的侨民，但由于他们无知，宁愿牺牲生命也不愿捐款。
幸而国内传来好消息。一两位热心人士慷慨解囊予以捐助，其他人也相继响应，但我们预计只能筹集到约三万美元，无望获得更多金额。
我们将于今日启程前往泗水（Si Seu 泗水），并将曾先生留在此处，试图说服一两位资本家。如果成功，可能会筹集到10万美元。
关于泗水（Si Seu 泗水）这个地方，我们获悉当地商会意图支持我们。
据此判断，我们有理由相信，在爪哇和其他港口，虽然大资本家不会掏腰包，但仍可筹集到约10万美元。但在我们抵达之前，无法确知确切情况。总之，此次我们访问英属和荷属殖民地的南方期间，可在一个月内筹集15万美元。
如果上海及其他地区发生起义，我们可以预见捐款将会源源不断。
访问泗水（Si Seu 泗水）后，我们打算返回新加坡，与卓文（Do Wen）商讨（钟智写信给我们说，卓文很快就会来新加坡），然后决定我们的行动。我们的意见是，长期滞留此地完全不宜。俗话说：“只能暂时做客，不能永久寄居。”如果我们久留，他人会感到不安，此外由于通讯不畅，我们无法得知祖国发生或正在发生的事情。如果我们回去也不好。狄引民（Tih Sun）已派遣许多人返回（?中国）。我们在此地漫游，既违背我们的意愿，也违背他人的意愿。
自从我们离开您后，尚未收到您来自内地的消息，对此我们深感遗憾。希望您收到此信后能给我们发一份电报。
也许，如果您命令我们回去，可能有助于唤醒民众，并促使他们寻找其他人来替代我们。
在英属殖民地筹集的捐款将寄往上海，而在荷属殖民地筹集的资金将寄往东京。
由于您始终与东京方面保持联系，您一定知晓一切。由于我们的行踪不定，我们无法向您倾诉所有想说的话。请见谅。
此致
敬礼。
铨（Ching 銓）和 智（Tsai 智）。

12月2日。
发自三宝垄。
